reason: This passage (Nehemiah 5) depicts internal Jewish economic hardship caused by exploitation among the Hebrew people themselves, not by divine antagonism. The text shows: (1) Nehemiah responding with compassion to the people's suffering; (2) ethical correction directed at the nobles and officials engaging in usury against their own people; (3) invocation of 'fear of God' (יראת אלהים) as a moral standard that should prevent such injustice; and (4) Nehemiah appealing to God to remember his righteous conduct. God is presented as a witness to justice and a rewarder of ethical behavior, not as antagonistic. The hardship stems from human exploitation and tribute payments to the Persian king, not from divine opposition to the Hebrew people.
